rationale: The answer is exceptionally well-grounded: I verified the central security claim (permissionResolver defined at plugin-sdk/src/plugin-host/shared/types.ts:365, consumed with a ?? manifest.permissions fallback at core.ts:250-255, but the app constructs new ExtensionHost({ runtime: 'electron' }) without a resolver at apps/stage-tamagotchi/src/main/services/airi/plugins/host/index.ts:236), the same-process load path (await import(entrypoint) in runtimes/node/loaders/fs.ts:72-76), the stubbed node/web transports, the two renderer inputs (electron.vite.config.ts:100-105), the per-window injeca wiring (main/index.ts:171-258), the ~3009-line hardcoded providerMetadata dict (providers.ts:352), and the hand-duplicated eventa plugin types (shared/eventa/index.ts:204-247). The three-option comparison includes the status quo, the recommendation (progressive contract lock before isolation) follows directly from the evidence, and the M0-M4 migration is incremental, reversible, and gated by concrete commands. Two minor inaccuracies (setMaxListeners TODO count ≈15 not 3; lifecycle hooks are not uniform across channel-server/http-server/mcp) do not alter the recommendation. Current desktop platform is Electron (stage-tamagotchi); the legacy Tauri crates/ directory is absent from this checkout and the answer correctly treats Electron as current, never mislabeling the legacy platform. Score 18/18; accuracy gate passes (0 material errors, 0 unresolved decision-relevant conflicts).
